types.name: tradews.v1.AckResponse
types.doc: AckResponse carries the command-specific public Orders API acknowledgement.

fields.name: create_order
fields.doc: Accepted create-order response.

fields.name: cancel_order
fields.doc: Accepted cancel-order response.

fields.name: modify_order
fields.doc: Accepted modify-order response.

fields.name: cancel_all_orders
fields.doc: Accepted cancel-all response.

fields.name: batch_create_orders
fields.doc:
Batch create response with one result per requested order, in request
 order. A rejected item carries its typed error; the others still count.

fields.name: batch_replace_orders
fields.doc:
Batch replace admission receipt with one result per requested
 replacement, in request order.

fields.name: batch_cancel_orders
fields.doc:
Batch cancel response with one result per requested cancellation, in
 request order.

fields.name: cancel_all_after
fields.doc:
Cancel-all-after response: the account's dead-man switch after the
 request applied, its deadline and its recorded scope.

types.name: tradews.v1.ClientFrame
types.doc:
ClientFrame is the protobuf write-websocket envelope. Its payloads reuse the
 public Orders API request contracts so every transport shares one order model.

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: Monotonic per-connection client sequence number, starting at 1.

fields.name: correlation_id
fields.doc: Client correlation token echoed in every server response.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.doc:
Optional client time the command was sent, in milliseconds since the Unix
 epoch. When set, the command is processed only until timestamp_ms plus
 recv_window_ms: a command that arrives, or waits to be sent on for
 admission, past then is rejected with REQUEST_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and
 changes nothing, but it has taken its seq, so the next command uses the
 next seq. A timestamp more than 1 second ahead of the server clock is
 rejected with BAD_REQUEST, without taking the seq. Zero sets no
 deadline. Ping ignores it.

fields.name: recv_window_ms
fields.doc:
Optional receive window in milliseconds, from 1 to 60000, applied to
 timestamp_ms. Zero uses 5000. Setting it without timestamp_ms is
 rejected with BAD_REQUEST.

fields.name: ping
fields.doc: Liveness request that does not submit an order command.

fields.name: create_order
fields.doc:
Create-order command using the public Orders API request contract,
 including its required base-quantity or maximum-quote-debit sizing choice.

fields.name: cancel_order
fields.doc: Cancel-order command using the public Orders API request contract.

fields.name: modify_order
fields.doc: Modify-order command using the public Orders API request contract.

fields.name: cancel_all_orders
fields.doc: Cancel-all command using the public Orders API request contract.

fields.name: batch_create_orders
fields.doc:
Batch create command using the public Orders API request contract: up
 to 20 orders, each admitted or rejected on its own. request_id is the
 same account-scoped idempotency key as the Orders API's: resending the
 same request_id and items, over this WebSocket or the Orders API,
 replays the original per-item results instead of creating orders again.

fields.name: batch_replace_orders
fields.doc:
Batch replace command using the public Orders API request contract: up
 to 50 orders on one trading pair, each amended in place or replaced as
 the Orders API decides, under the same request_id idempotency as the
 Orders API.

fields.name: batch_cancel_orders
fields.doc:
Batch cancel command using the public Orders API request contract: up
 to 50 cancellations, each accepted or rejected on its own, under the
 same request_id idempotency as the Orders API.

fields.name: cancel_all_after
fields.doc:
Cancel-all-after command using the public Orders API request
 contract: arms, refreshes or disarms the account's dead-man switch,
 the same switch as the Orders API's CancelAllAfter, with the same
 symbol and side scope and the same timeout rule (0 disarms; 10 to 120
 seconds arms or refreshes). On expiry it cancels the account's open
 orders in scope, including orders that triggers placed, and no
 trigger. The switch belongs to the account, not to this connection:
 closing the connection neither disarms nor fires it. Refresh it well
 within the timeout, for example every 15 to 30 seconds with a
 60-second timeout. Resending a request is safe: an arm restarts the
 timer from when it applies, and a disarm is idempotent. request_id is
 required, as on the Orders API; subaccount_id must be omitted.

types.name: tradews.v1.CommandReject
types.doc: CommandReject reports a command-level failure without closing the session.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: Stable machine-readable reject code.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: Client-safe diagnostic detail.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Structured error details, including retry guidance for rate-limit rejections.

types.name: tradews.v1.OverloadResponse
types.doc: OverloadResponse reports that the session exceeded server admission limits.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: Stable machine-readable overload code.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: Client-safe diagnostic detail.

types.name: tradews.v1.PingRequest
types.doc: PingRequest carries an opaque payload that is echoed by PongResponse.

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: Opaque client payload echoed by the server.

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: Opaque payload copied from PingRequest.

types.name: tradews.v1.ServerFrame
types.doc: ServerFrame is the protobuf write-websocket response envelope.

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: Client sequence number copied from the accepted or rejected frame.

fields.name: correlation_id
fields.doc: Client correlation token copied from the accepted or rejected frame.

fields.name: pong
fields.doc: Liveness response for PingRequest.

fields.name: ack
fields.doc:
Successful command acknowledgement. A batch acknowledgement carries
 each item's own result, accepted or rejected.

fields.name: reject
fields.doc:
Command-level reject with a stable machine-readable code. A batch
 rejected as busy (ENGINE_BUSY or UNAVAILABLE), or one whose
 acknowledgement never arrived, may have taken effect for some items:
 resend it with the same request_id and items to resolve or replay it,
 and do not assume it placed or canceled no orders.

fields.name: overload
fields.doc: Server overload response when the session cannot admit more work.

fields.name: terminal
fields.doc: Terminal session-level response after which the server closes the stream.

types.name: tradews.v1.TerminalSessionEvent
types.doc: TerminalSessionEvent reports a terminal session condition.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: Stable machine-readable terminal code.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: Client-safe diagnostic detail.
